citation.quote: Stay off its inside, keep it between us, and we wear it down.

content.value: Per Aria's read: the Doorward is slow off the wall but hits like the wall it came out of (heavy, hard-hitting). A low seam sits on its pale chest where the plaster closed over itself — 'might be soft,' but she can't be certain from range. Her tactics: stay off its inside, keep it between the two of them, and wear it down. This is a fight to be won by positioning and attrition, not a puzzle to be solved.

citation.quote: the far end, and the thing the far end was built to make you earn.

content.summary: The far shut door opened onto the floor's first challenge, founded as COMBAT: the Doorward — a heavy dead-white plaster construct that aggresses, slow but hard-hitting, with a possibly-soft chest seam — must be worn down by Alan (empty-handed) and Aria (Hotel-fitted to his measure) keeping it between them. Per the hotel's premise, clearing it climbs the floor. The fight is joined.

citation.quote: Whatever the Hotel means to test here, it was never the door.

content.event: Alan and Aria go down the cold end of the hall (past his door and her grown room) to the shut door that has hung dark since he woke, and open it — it is only a door, and swings silent. The cold chamber beyond is not empty.

citation.quote: one man, empty-handed, nothing on you but the clothes you woke in.

content.value: Alan meets the Doorward as he is — one man, empty-handed, with nothing on him but the clothes he woke in. He carries no weapon and no object into the fight.

citation.quote: the Hotel that fits a room to its guest has fitted her to your measure tonight

content.value: For the Doorward fight the Hotel — which fits a room to its guest — has fitted Aria to Alan's measure: the two of them are now the same size as each other. She carries the change like she has decided not to mind it, and fights at his scale.

citation.quote: The Doorward stands up out of the far wall as you cross the sill — the same dead-white plaster the whole place is grown from, pulling itself whole and upright, a heavy blank body a head taller than you and built wide

content.value: The Doorward is the floor-1 challenge: a construct that stands up out of the far chamber's wall — the same dead-white plaster the whole Hotel is grown from — a heavy blank body a head taller than Alan and built wide. Unlike a passive lock, it aggresses: it does not wait to be looked at but turns on Alan and Aria 'with the slow certainty of a thing with one job and the mass to do it.'

citation.quote: The Doorward takes its first heavy step, and the cold room narrows to the space between you and it.

content.event: The Doorward stands up out of the far wall — a head taller, built wide, heavy — and turns on them without waiting. Aria, fitted to Alan's measure, calls the tactics (wear it down, keep it between them). The Doorward takes its first heavy step and the fight begins, Alan facing it empty-handed.

citation.quote: The part that keeps a thing true when it would be easier not to.

content.value: Aria's LINK binding takes Alan's truth-keeping — the part of him that holds its ground and keeps a thing true when it would be easier not to (explicitly not his cleverness, which she declined).

citation.quote: you've got the claws for it, aim for the seam.

content.value: Tall and visibly draconic: silver-white hair; pale silver-grey round-pupiled eyes; a scatter of pale scales high on each cheekbone; two dark horns swept back off her brow; silver tracery running the length of her body; and clawed hands (talons) she can fight with. Usually in deep sapphire silk off one shoulder, silver at her wrist. Her claws are part of her nature, not her gear — they persist in the Hotel's size-fitted combat form (the down-scaling changes her size, not her claws).

citation.quote: the trick is to be worth hitting and never be where the hit lands.

content.event: Alan calls the play — he'll bait, Aria strikes the seam. He breaks for the Doorward loud and wide open; it turns and hurls a fast pale-slab arm at his head; he drops out of reach clean, the blow shearing the air a hand from his face (no damage, a near thing). He gives ground and circles, and the construct drags after him, its blind flank opening to the room.

citation.quote: the seam opens under her hand, and a long crack runs up from it with a sound like a flagstone splitting.

content.value: The low chest seam IS the Doorward's vulnerability — confirmed by action, not oracle: Aria's t13 hedge ('might be soft') was borne out when her claws found it and it GAVE, a long crack splitting up the construct where the warded mass otherwise turns every blow aside. It is slow off the wall but its arms swing fast and hit hard; the way to reach the seam is to bait its attention (Alan) and strike the exposed flank (Aria), keeping it between them. It is big: one crack will not fell it — it must be worn down by repeated seam-hits.

citation.quote: this time there is no might-be about it. It gives.

content.event: In the opening Alan bought, Aria goes in low and fast with her claws and finds the low seam — and it gives, a long crack splitting up the construct with a sound like a flagstone breaking. First true damage to the Doorward; it lurches. But it is a big thing and one crack will not fell it: it wrenches up, slower now and favoring the cracked side, still square between the two of them and the door it keeps. The fight continues.

citation.quote: The thing will not leave the doorway — cannot; guarding it is all it's for

content.value: The Doorward is the floor-1 challenge: a construct that stands up out of the far chamber's wall — the same dead-white plaster the whole Hotel is grown from — a heavy blank body a head taller than Alan and built wide. Unlike a passive lock it aggresses, turning on them with the slow certainty of a thing with one job and the mass to do it. It is DOOR-BOUND: it will not — cannot — leave the doorway, because guarding the door is the whole of what it is for. This makes the door itself the ground any fight with it is fought on.

citation.quote: The thing has kept the one lesson the last pass taught it — it holds the cracked side turned inward, hunched toward the wall, and gives Aria the flat of its warded shoulder instead

content.value: The low chest seam is the Doorward's vulnerability — confirmed by action at t14, where a clawed strike to the seam opened it while the warded mass turns every other blow aside. It is slow off the wall but its arms swing fast and hard. The reachable way in is to bait its attention (Alan) and strike the exposed flank (Aria). BUT it guards its known wound: once the seam is opened, it keeps the cracked side turned to the wall and presents only warded shoulder, so a REPEAT of the exact same bait-and-strike is countered (claws skid off warded plaster, no purchase). Reaching the seam again takes a NEW opening or angle, not a repeat of the last. Its adaptation is narrow — it protects the wound; it does not otherwise get cleverer.

citation.quote: "It's got wise to that," she says, landing back at your shoulder.

content.event: First setback. Alan makes the guarded door his ground (the Doorward cannot leave it) and works the same bait, meaning to swing the cracked side back into Aria's reach. But the Doorward has learned — it holds the cracked side to the wall and gives Aria only warded shoulder. Her seam-strike finds nothing to open; claws skid off the hard mass, no purchase, and she pulls back clean before the arm comes round. No crack this pass. It draws square to the door, cracked side to the wall, and holds — watching for what they try next. The repeat tactic is spent; a new angle is needed.

citation.quote: a thread — you could not say where it runs or how, only that it is there, drawn taut and live between the two of you

content.event: THE LINK's first bind is made, mutual and complete — Alan binds Aria's plain force, Aria binds Alan's truth-keeping — and manifests as a live thread drawn taut between them, each able to feel the far end living in the other.

citation.quote: It is the plain force of her: the fact of the whole strange night bending itself around her without her seeming to ask it to. That. You reach for it, and you tell the pane so.

content.value: Alan's LINK binding takes Aria's plain, unarguable force — the way the whole night bends itself around her without her seeming to ask it to.

citation.quote: drawn taut and live between the two of you

content.summary: THE LINK's first bind is made and mutual: Alan bound Aria's plain force, Aria bound Alan's truth-keeping. A live thread now runs between them; each bound trait rises as its source rises. (What further activations or additional binds THE LINK allows remains unseen.)

citation.quote: she is moving before you are, down the hall toward the door you have not opened, one hand held back for yours.

content.event: The System points them toward the far shut door at the dark end of the hall; Aria re-gowns, her ease giving way to the alertness she wore in the hallway, and leads Alan down toward the door they have not opened.

citation.quote: The seam gives all the way, a second split forking off the first, and the Doorward buckles at the middle and rocks back a full step, its heels scraping over the sill of the door it guards.

content.event: Aria strikes into the crack Alan tore wide — low and hard, her claws in the soft of it — and the seam gives all the way, a second split forking off the first. The Doorward buckles at the middle and rocks back a full step, its heels scraping over the sill of the door it guards. Heavy damage; its guard is failing and it is driven back onto the threshold.

citation.quote: You break the circle the other way.

content.event: Alan finds the new angle: he reverses his circling direction to catch the Doorward's learned pivot committed wrong, and its guarded side swings open. He goes inside the reach and drives the heel of his hand into the seam himself — no claws, a lesser blow than Aria's, but the crack takes it and splits a shade wider, cold pouring out. Too close now, he throws himself clear, rolling under the baited arm as it cracks into the floor where he stood — the seam left open behind him.

citation.quote: You are inside its guard before it can, everything you have thrown high — your shoulder into the cracked chest, driving up and back to take it down with you.

content.event: Pressing the buckling Doorward before it can find footing off its lost sill, Alan goes inside its guard and drives his shoulder into the cracked chest, taking the far-heavier construct down with him — they crash together on the cold floor. But it does not go down alone: its vast arms close around him as they land, pinning one arm to his side and crushing the air out of him. Alan is now inside its reach with no way back out, the grip only tightening.

citation.quote: Her claws go into the crack to the knuckle and tear, and the Doorward answers it — a deep grinding shudder runs through it, the split running wider, something structural giving behind the plaster.

content.event: With Alan pinned and the fall having turned the split seam up to her, Aria reaches past his cheek into the open seam a hand's breadth from where he is held — claws to the knuckle — and tears. The Doorward convulses: a deep grinding shudder runs through it, the split running wider, something structural giving behind the plaster. Its crushing grip loosens for the first time since it closed, slackening as the thing convulses around its wound.

citation.quote: they clamp you to the pale mass as you land, pinning one arm to your side, crushing the air out of you

content.value: The low chest seam is the Doorward's vulnerability — confirmed by action at t14, where a clawed strike to the seam opened it while the warded mass turns every other blow aside. It is slow off the wall but its arms swing fast and hard. The reachable way in is to bait its attention (Alan) and strike the exposed flank (Aria). BUT it guards its known wound: once the seam is opened, it keeps the cracked side turned to the wall and presents only warded shoulder, so a REPEAT of the exact same bait-and-strike is countered (claws skid off warded plaster, no purchase). Reaching the seam again takes a NEW opening or angle, not a repeat of the last. Its adaptation is narrow — it protects the wound; it does not otherwise get cleverer. AND it grapples: any fighter caught inside its reach is seized and pinned by its vast arms and crushed — the lethal line — so the close-in game is its own danger, not merely the path to the seam. This surfaced at t17 when Alan took it down body-to-body and its arms clamped him to the pale mass as they landed, pinning one arm and crushing the air out of him with no way back out.

citation.quote: you close your fingers on the haft and work it loose — a knife, slim and plain and cold, no longer than your hand

content.value: Alan entered the Doorward fight empty-handed, but at the clear he drew a weapon from its bared keystone core: a knife, slim and plain and cold, no longer than his hand. He knows what it is for 'as surely as [he has] known nothing else in this place,' and it was the blade that stopped the construct. It is his first weapon in the Hotel — the one edged thing the wall was hiding — and he keeps it after the fight (the floor rises leaving 'nothing on the floor but you and the knife and Aria').

citation.quote: And the Doorward stops. The grinding, the shudder, the vast grip on your arm — gone, cut clean, the straining mass gone still around you.

content.event: Knowing what it is for, Alan turns the knife in his fist and drives it back into the keystone it came from — the blade finds the fault and goes home. The Doorward stops dead: the grinding, the shudder, and the crushing grip on his arm all cut clean, the mass gone still with the knife buried to its hilt, and it does not move again. Then the pale plaster loosens and draws back into the wall it grew from, until nothing is left on the floor but Alan, the knife, and Aria. The floor-1 challenge is defeated.

citation.quote: the floor itself takes a breath — a long slow lift through the soles and the spine, the light along the walls sliding a shade warmer as the whole floor climbs

content.event: With the Doorward gone, the floor itself lifts — a long slow climb felt through the soles and the spine, the wall-light sliding a shade warmer as the whole floor rises. When it settles the cold chamber is folded away behind them and the hall runs on ahead, longer and darker at its far end, where a new shut door has grown where the wall had run unbroken before. Clearing the challenge climbed the floor and seeded the next.

citation.quote: she straightens up out of the wreck of the fight more easily than she should, standing into the space a shade more solidly than she had this morning, steadier on the follow-through

content.event: In the climb Aria comes out subtly changed — nothing so plain as taller, but she straightens out of the fight's wreck more easily than she should, standing into the space a shade more solidly than she had that morning and steadier on the follow-through, as if the same step that lifted Alan loosed something in her that had been held tight. Alan sees it take, marks it, and sets it aside.

citation.quote: the white mass loosening and drawing back into the wall it grew from, until there is nothing on the floor but you and the knife and Aria

content.summary: The floor's first challenge — the Doorward — is CLEARED. Worn down at its chest seam by Alan's baiting and Aria's clawed strikes, then finished when the seam was torn to its keystone core, a keystone-seated blade drawn, and driven home into the fault: the construct stopped dead and drew back into the wall it grew from. Per the Hotel's premise, clearing it climbed the floor (the whole floor rose, the cold chamber folded away, a new shut door grew at the hall's far end).

citation.quote: you close your fingers on the haft and work it loose — a knife, slim and plain and cold, no longer than your hand

content.value: The keystone knife is the slim, plain, cold blade — no longer than Alan's hand — that was seated in the Doorward's keystone core, 'as though the hall had set it there and grown the guard up around it,' and drawn by Alan at the floor-1 clear (t18). It is the weapon that stopped the construct: driven back home into the keystone fault, it cut the Doorward still. Alan 'knows what it is for as surely as [he has] known nothing else in this place.' It is now his standing weapon and his first in the Hotel — see ent-alan inventory (ent-alan-armed). (Its design name and combat properties are the loremaker's sheet-truth, not asserted here.)

citation.quote: you drive down with everything left to you: your shoulder, your free hand, all your slight weight bearing the cracked mass low, holding its blank attention on you and off the woman at its flank

content.event: The clear is a co-op finish. Still pinned with one arm caught, Alan tells Aria 'Don't stop' and drives down with everything left to him — shoulder, free hand, and all his slight weight — bearing the cracked Doorward low and holding its blank attention on himself and off Aria at its flank; and it stays down. With the construct held, Aria's sustained tearing at the split (claws in the crack to the wrist) widens it past what the plaster can draw shut, until the wound opens all the way to the hard pale core it was poured around: the keystone, bared at last. A blade sits seated in that core; the free hand Alan is bearing down with is a span away, and he closes his fingers on the haft and works it loose — a knife, slim and plain and cold, no longer than his hand.

citation.quote: A bed, a basin, a lamp, linens folded by hands you never saw. Nothing with an edge to it, nothing that answers to weapon or key.

content.event: After the clear, Alan calls a stop — 'We should stop. Both of us.' — and Aria, her brightness banked low, agrees. He explores the new (second) floor's lived-in near end: a suite that is somehow his, made up as though it had been waiting on him, and past it a smaller silver-grey room that must be Aria's. Both hold only ordinary rest furniture — a bed, a basin, a lamp, folded linens — nothing with an edge, nothing that answers to weapon or key. He sets the keystone knife on the table by the bed and lies down; the fight's toll eases by degrees as full rest restores them both.

citation.quote: The floor keeps its useful things behind its doors, you are starting to see, and pays them out only to those who get through

content.value: The Hotel's economy of gear, as Alan is starting to see it: the floor keeps its useful things behind its challenges and pays them out only to those who get through. Borne out so far — floor 1 yielded the keystone knife only at the Doorward clear, while the residential (lived-in) end of a floor holds only the ordinary furniture of rest (bed, basin, lamp, linens) — nothing with an edge, nothing that answers to weapon or key. Loot is earned past a challenge, not found at rest.

citation.quote: the thread that runs between you lies a little nearer the surface than it did this morning, close enough to feel if you turn toward it

content.event: Having gone into the moving-plaster fight together and come out the other side, Alan and Aria find the LINK thread between them lies nearer the surface than it did that morning — close enough to feel if he turns toward it. Neither reaches for more than closeness tonight; the fight is too near. Aria bids him sleep in her old low voice, naming the place a dungeon that is 'very good at waiting' — and at the dark far end of the hall, the new challenge door waits with it.

citation.quote: I have no luck to give you, you know. It is not a thing I deal in — no one does; the dice fall where they fall, and I would be lying if I told you my hands could tip them.

content.value: Aria will not claim she can confer luck. When Alan asks to 'fuck for luck' before the next door, she honestly refuses the charm: she has no luck to give, it is not a thing she deals in, and 'the dice fall where they fall' — she would be lying to say her hands could tip them. She takes the intimacy gladly and for its own sake, explicitly 'not because it buys you anything at that door,' and afterward tells him he is 'no luckier than you were, but better company for the walk.' Consistent with the truth-keeping trait she bound off Alan: she does not sell comfort she cannot make true. (Narrative stance disclosed in prose; any luck/outcome mechanics are the loremaker's sheet-truth.)

citation.quote: It never spoke to me before. Not once, in all my years.

content.value: The System's pane spoke and showed only to Alan through the first night; at THE LINK's first activation it addresses Aria as well — by her account the first time it has ever spoken to her.

citation.quote: you feel Aria go rigid against your chest

content.value: The companion's name is Aria (first spoken in the narration at turn-10).

citation.quote: It wants me to give you a piece of me. And to take a piece of you in return.

content.event: At THE LINK's activation the System addresses Aria directly for the first time, prompting her to choose too — she must give Alan a piece of herself and take a piece of him in return; the bind is mutual.

citation.quote: It is talking to her now.

content.summary: The System, which had only ever addressed Alan, speaks to Aria for the first time in all her years at THE LINK's first activation. Why it opened to her now — and precisely what THE LINK is — is the new open question.

citation.quote: As if I hadn't done this before." Her eyes come up. "I hadn't. Not once. Not this."

content.value: Despite three thousand years, Aria says she has never done 'this' before — never before wanted someone she wished to slow down for, nor anything she did not want to be finished with.

citation.quote: Selection required.

content.summary: THE LINK awaits its first binding — a MUTUAL bind: Alan selects one of Aria's skills/attributes and she selects one of his, each bound trait rising as its source rises. As of turn-10 both of them now see the prompt; selection pending on both sides.

citation.quote: Talent — first activation.

content.event: The System names Alan's Talent for the first time — THE LINK — and stops, awaiting his selection. (The NIGHT/FULL award beats render as typed System window-beats, not prose.)

citation.quote: She reaches between you and takes you in her hand and guides you to her, and sinks down — slow, an inch, and stops, and breathes, and takes another inch, until she has taken all of you

content.event: Alan and Aria sleep together; she takes him astride, seating him deep and insisting on a slow, deliberate pace — her first time wanting to make anything last.

citation.quote: "I don't take its notes. It doesn't get to call this one."

content.line: I don't take its notes. It doesn't get to call this one.
content.speaker: aria

citation.quote: has the look of somewhere that wants something from you before it opens

content.summary: The far shut door at the dark end of the hall — the 'adventure' way — looks as if it wants something of Alan before it opens; still unentered.

citation.quote: a second doorway pressing itself out of flat plaster, molding and lintel and all, as if the corridor had recalled it wanted one more room here and simply put one in.

content.value: The hotel's walls grow rooms and doorways on demand — a doorway (and the room behind it) can press itself out of flat plaster where none was.

citation.quote: One moment there is no you at all. Then there is: flat on your back on a floor that is cool and close-carpeted

content.event: Alan comes into being at the bottom of the Harem Hotel with no memory of arriving; the System pane measures his soul and goes still.

citation.quote: A woman comes out of it.

content.event: The wall grows a doorway and a woman (Aria) steps out of it, greeting Alan where he lies.

citation.quote: the name of the place — the Harem Hotel — and its floor, and the floor is the first.

content.value: The place is named the Harem Hotel; Alan wakes on its first floor (the floor is the first).

citation.quote: until you are both standing, close, closer than the leverage strictly needed, and you have not let go of her hand.

content.event: Alan takes Aria's offered hand and rises; they stand close and keep the hold.

citation.quote: I came into this place much the way you seem to have — elsewhere one moment, here the next, no door behind me I can point to

content.value: Arrived in the hotel much as Alan did — elsewhere one moment, here the next, no door behind her; her memory-blank matches his.

citation.quote: You woke with the front of your life torn off; I can't tell you what tore it

content.summary: What tore off the front of Alan's life and brought him to the hotel — his amnesia's cause — remains unknown.

citation.quote: No ceremony to it — it states what you crossed and what the crossing paid you, the way a ledger states a sum, and goes quiet.

content.event: After the kiss the System delivers a flat, ceremony-less readout of what Alan crossed and what the crossing paid, then goes quiet. (The awarded values render as typed System window-beats, not prose.)

citation.quote: Behind you, without a sound, the door eases itself shut on the hall.

content.event: Alan chooses the near open door and draws Aria into the room made to his taste; the door shuts itself and a new System pane appears.

citation.quote: "So it talks to you, and not to me," she says, quiet, working it as she goes.

content.value: Only Alan can see the System pane; his companion cannot — it speaks to him and not to her.

citation.quote: Two people at the bottom of a thing neither can name past its name.

content.summary: The nature and logic of the Harem Hotel — why it exists, what it wants — is unknown to both Alan and Aria; it has not explained itself.

citation.quote: No door you came through. No before.

content.value: Alan woke at the bottom of the hotel with no memory of arriving — no door he came through, no before.

citation.quote: For one blank second you don't have your own name, and then you do — *Alan* — and it arrives clean and sure and fastened to absolutely nothing else.

content.value: The protagonist's name is Alan — it arrives on waking, fastened to nothing else.

citation.quote: Low on the pane, one line where a value should sit stays blank.

content.value: unknown — at first measurement the System pane leaves Alan's Talent line blank (not zero, not hidden; simply empty).

citation.quote: Bind one of her skills or attributes. She binds one of yours. A bound trait rises as its source rises.

content.value: THE LINK — Alan's Talent, first activated after the night with Aria: bind one of her skills or attributes and she binds one of yours; a bound trait rises as its source rises. Selection required.

citation.quote: "Three thousand years I've decided when the scene gets warm," she says at last, low.

content.value: By her own account roughly three thousand years old.

citation.quote: deep sapphire silk off the one shoulder, a thread of silver at her wrist. Silver-white hair. A scatter of pale scales high on each cheekbone catching the low light, and two dark horns swept back off her brow

content.value: Tall; silver-white hair; pale silver-grey round-pupiled eyes; a scatter of pale scales high on each cheekbone; two dark horns swept back off her brow; deep sapphire silk off one shoulder, silver at her wrist. Silver tracery runs the length of her body under the gown.

citation.quote: The other way the hall runs on, and narrows, and darkens toward a single shut door at the very end

content.value: The first-floor hallway runs two ways from where Alan wakes: a near end with a wide open warm door onto a room made for him, and a far end that narrows and darkens toward a single shut door at the very end.

citation.quote: "I got no message."

content.summary: Why the System pane is visible and speaks only to Alan, never to Aria, is an open mystery.

citation.quote: it is furnished like somewhere you already live. The bed is made, and made to your taste.

content.value: The near room is furnished exactly to Alan's taste — bed, light, and reading-chair placed as if someone had watched him live, though no one has.

citation.quote: "Keep it exactly this true," she says. "Whatever I make of it after — and I will, I always do — don't let me. Just this. Just what it actually was, and not the lovelier thing I turn it into."

content.line: Keep it exactly this true. Whatever I make of it after — and I will, I always do — don't let me. Just this. Just what it actually was, and not the lovelier thing I turn it into.
content.speaker: aria

citation.quote: But you are not doing this alone — that part I can make true just by staying.

content.event: Aria admits she knows no more of the place than Alan does, but commits to staying with him — 'you are not doing this alone.'

citation.quote: To close the distance between us.

content.event: The System issues Alan its first quest — to close the distance between him and Aria; Aria receives no message and learns the System speaks only to him.

citation.quote: You close the gap once again, all the way this time, and kiss her, slow — no rush anywhere in it.

content.event: Alan and Aria kiss, slow and unhurried.

citation.quote: You dress. You take up the knife. You go to see what the second floor has grown to stop you.

content.event: Alan wakes on the second floor all at once and whole — no ache, no ghost of the fight — the rest having fully restored him. Where the night before he could not have looked at the dark far end of the hall without flinching, this morning he can. Aria rises first, gathers herself back into her composed silver shape, and hands him his shirt. He dresses, takes up the keystone knife from the bedside table, and goes to see what the second floor has grown to stop him.

citation.quote: It is not the careful, astonished thing the first night was; you know each other now, the map of it, what she likes and how she likes to be made to wait for it.

content.event: In the morning Alan and Aria are intimate a second time — no longer the careful, astonished thing the first night (turn-10) was, but known and easy now, Aria setting the pace and making him wait. It is taken for its own sake, not as a luck-charm. A relational deepening only — nothing numeric, no bind change; the thread between them is felt, not spent.

citation.quote: Hers hang where she can see them and you cannot; yours where you can and she cannot.

content.value: Each person's System pane is private to them — Aria's letters hang where only she can read them and Alan cannot, and his where only he can and she cannot.

citation.quote: the two of you become — for the first time — two people reading the air at once

content.event: For the first time Alan and Aria read their own System panes at once — each seeing only their own. Aria, never before addressed by it, invites Alan to lead THE LINK's mutual selection; the turn ends on the open prompt, unanswered.

citation.quote: She gets the shirt down your arms and off, and drops it without looking where it falls.

content.value: The only garment ever named on Alan is a shirt — Aria opened its front and drew it off him during the night (turn-10), dropping it on the floor of his suite. No lower-body clothing, footwear, or other garment has been described, and turn-1 does not detail what he woke in. His skin bears no markings, unlike Aria's silver tracery.
